question: Türkiye has just announced defence agreements with Somalia and Djibouti, which will include the provision of arms, ships and training. Somalia has also concluded a defence agreement with Qatar. 1.

In the light of Ethiopia’s recent agreement with Somaliland, does the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy consider that the risk of conflict in the Horn of Africa has risen sharply?

Can the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy please provide an assessment of how Türkiye’s provision of maritime assets will impact the activity of the Houthi regime in Yemen?
answer: The Memorandum of Understanding announced on 1 January 2024 between Ethiopia and Somaliland has contributed to a rise in tensions in the region. The EU supports the unity, the sovereignty, and the territorial integrity of the countries of the region, including Somalia, pursuant to their constitutions, the Charters of the African Union and the United Nations.

This is key for the peace and stability of the entire Horn of Africa. It is imperative that Ethiopia and Somalia engage in dialogue to resolve their issues. It is also of paramount importance that other actors in the region contribute to de-escalation and reducing tensions.

In this regard, the European Council has underlined in the Council Conclusions of June 2021 its expectation from Türkiye and all actors to contribute positively to the resolution of regional crises (1). Since the agreement is not public, it is currently not possible to assess of how it will impact the activity of the Houthi regime in Yemen.
